title: Rosalind and the Ghost
premise: August Delacroix, a peace-delegation interpreter in a fractured border city, receives calls on a burner phone from Rosalind Vane—a colleague officially dead for two years—claiming she is alive, hunted, and ready to expose the delegation's secret complicity in war crimes. Extracting her means betraying the institution that gave him purpose and trusting a woman whose 'death' he may have helped stage without knowing it. As the delegation's security chief closes in and the evidence Rosalind carries proves both their salvation and their death sentence, August must choose between loyalty to the mission and the truth it buried. In the end, August smuggles Rosalind's testimony out at the cost of his own cover, and the two go underground together as the delegation collapses under the revelations.
about_author: Juniper Thackeray is the pen name of a former humanitarian logistics coordinator who spent six years in contested border regions before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people trapped between institutions and their consciences.

chapters.title: The Dead Frequency
chapters.summary: POV August. During a stalled ceasefire session, August interprets a negotiation he knows is theater, then finds a burner phone sewn into his coat lining. It rings; the voice is Rosalind Vane's—the interpreter who died in a shelling two years ago. The beat: dread laced with impossible hope.

chapters.title: Rules of Invisibility
chapters.summary: POV August. Flashback-tinged chapter establishing how August learned to survive by obeying rewritten rules after Rosalind's death was ruled an accident he witnessed but was ordered to forget. Security chief Ilsa Brandt begins quietly auditing staff movements. The beat: suffocating caution.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: POV August. Following Rosalind's instructions to a flooded quarry outside the city, August finds her cache: documents implicating the delegation's leadership in trading ceasefire corridors for arms shipments. A second phone call warns him he was followed. The beat: vertigo of complicity.

chapters.title: Ilsa
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Brandt. The security chief interrogates a junior staffer about missing inventory, revealing she has her own private file on Rosalind's death—and doubts of her own. She suspects a leak but not yet August. The beat: menace with a crack of humanity.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: POV August. Rosalind agrees to meet at a tram depot, but August realizes the extraction route she proposes passes exactly where the delegation's signals team detected anomalies. Is she the defector or the lure? He goes anyway. The beat: suspicion sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Tram 9, Last Service
chapters.summary: POV August. The meeting happens: Rosalind is real, scarred, and furious that August took three years to look. She explains she faked her death when she discovered the corridor deal, but admits someone fed her August's name—which she never gave them. The beat: reunion poisoned by doubt.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Brandt decodes the anomaly pattern and identifies the burner network—then discovers her superior ordered the audit suppressed. She realizes she is being managed too, and makes a quiet copy of her Rosalind file. The beat: an ally born from betrayal.

chapters.title: Corridor of Ash
chapters.summary: POV August. The extraction through the demilitarized corridor goes wrong; a strike hits on schedule, proving the route was leaked—by Rosalind's handler, who wanted the documents destroyed with witnesses. August and Rosalind escape wounded into the tunnels beneath the old quarter. The beat: betrayal confirmed, trust reforged.

chapters.title: Everything We Buried
chapters.summary: POV August and Ilsa alternating. In the tunnels, Rosalind reveals August signed the transit manifest that moved the arms—he was the unwitting instrument all along. Ilsa arrives not to arrest them but to hand over her file and open the delegation's secure uplink. The beat: guilt confronted, alliance sealed.

chapters.title: Rosalind and the Ghost
chapters.summary: POV August. Using the uplink, they broadcast the testimony during the delegation's final plenary; the room detonates, arrests begin, and August burns his own credentials on-air, naming himself among the culpable. Weeks later, underground and anonymous, he and Rosalind plan what justice looks like next. The beat: costly, hard-won peace.
